messages:
maria: Quick follow-up to the on‑prem/air‑gapped packaging RFC — I sketched three delivery options and we should pick one to put into the runbook. TL;DR: (A) full immutable appliance image, (B) delta patch bundles + agent, (C) declarative manifest + customer registry pull. Pros/cons below, need engineering tradeoffs and rollout plan.

samir: Agree we should decide soon. My vote is (B) because clients often want smaller downloads and ability to apply security-only hotfixes.

jess: Curious about DB migrations in (B). How do we guarantee atomic upgrade for schema changes?

maria: Good point. For (B) I propose a two-phase migration: 1) schema-additive migrations shipped first with feature-flag gate, 2) backfill step as separate job. If we need breaking changes, require a maintenance window and full backup/restore fallback.

kai: For (A) appliance image — simplest rollback (revert to previous image) but large bundle size and slow airgap distribution. Also more opaque for customers.

samir: Another tricky one is verification. Air-gapped customers need strong signing + reproducible builds. We should include sigstore-style signatures or vendor-signed attestations.

jess: We also need preflight checks to avoid bricking. Can we run a local dry-run that verifies disk space, expected kernel modules, and free GPU memory before applying patch?

maria: Yes. Adding a preflight step is mandatory. Draft preflight script:```bash
#!/bin/bash
# preflight checks
free_bytes=$(df --output=avail /var | tail -1)
if [ $free_bytes -lt 1048576 ]; then echo "not enough disk"; exit 1; fi
# check service health endpoints
curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:8080/health || exit 2
# check model cache size
# ...
```
This runs locally and produces a short diagnostics bundle for support if it fails.

samir: I like the diagnostics bundle. We should standardize the format (jsonl) so the console and support tools can parse it.

kai: Operationally: (C) manifest + registry is elegant but requires customer infra to host images. For some regulated customers that’s fine, but many want us to handle the bundle delivery.

jess: For compatibility surface, we need a clear matrix: runtime version -> model format -> KV cache layout. If we change cache format we must support migration or invalidate cache safely.

maria: Proposed decision: Default offering = (B) delta patch bundles applied by our agent with strict signing and preflight checks. Offer (A) as an optional appliance for customers who prefer full images. (C) optional for enterprises that host registries. Thoughts? :thinking_face: 

samir: :thumbsup: I support. Implementation items: bundle format (tar.gz with manifest.json + signatures), agent CLI mode for "apply"/"rollback", and a server-side tool to compose deltas.

jess: Add a special flag for DB-breaking upgrades: --maintenance-window=ISO8601 and require operator confirmation in the console. Also a dry-run mode that simulates migrations.

sre-oncall: From SRE perspective, add a safe fallback: if post-upgrade health check fails within X minutes, agent should automatically roll back to previous good bundle. Also emit metrics to our telemetry endpoint when agent performs upgrades.

maria: Rollback plan: agent keeps last two bootable snapshots, stores incremental metadata under /var/lib/redwood/agent/versions. Rollback command: `redwood-agent rollback --to <version>` — agent verifies signatures before switching.

kai: Network transport options for airgap: USB bundle, scp via bastion, or local registry import. We should document exact expected file names and checksums to remove ambiguity.

samir: Security: HSM/KMS signing is required for enterprise; for small customers we can use vendor-signed certs but document threat model. Also add an offline verification tool for auditors.

jess: One more: can we reuse the private control plane to orchestrate staged rollouts for Dedicated customers? Means less agent complexity if control plane issues a "apply" token.

maria: We can. For hosted/dedicated customers control plane issues short-lived signed tokens and bundle URIs. For air-gapped customers we fall back to offline bundles. We'll include both flows in the runbook.

sre-oncall: Final: schedule a canary in a test cluster (lab) and an internal GtM run before cutting a GA. Also set the alert threshold for upgrade failure rate > 1% to block subsequent batches.

maria: Thanks — I'll update the RFC with these decisions and a first-draft runbook section. Anyone want to pick owner for the agent + signing work?

samir: I can take the agent side (apply/rollback + preflight).

jess: I'll own migrations & dry-run tooling.

kai: I'll write up transport options and appliance image spec.

maria: Awesome. I'll push the updated RFC and tag owners. deploy-bot: please create issue cards for agent, migrations, transport, docs.

deploy-bot: Created issues: #4123 (agent up/down), #4124 (migrations dry-run), #4125 (airgap transport), #4126 (runbook docs) — assigned to samir/jess/kai/maria.

maria: OK closing thread — I'll ping once RFC PR is up. Thanks all. :party_popper:
